title: Rust: Virtual Machine
description: Build a more complete virtual machine with control flow, functions, and memory.

steps.title: Control Flow: Jump and JumpIf
steps.description: Add `Jump(usize)` and `JumpIfZero(usize)` opcodes. Create a program that loops: push 10, decrement, print, jump if not zero back to start.
hints: `JumpIfZero(addr)`: pop top, if zero (or false), jump to addr.

verification.failureMessage: Run a countdown loop from 10 to 1.

steps.title: Comparison Operations
steps.description: Add opcodes: `LessThan`, `GreaterThan`, `Equal`, `Not`. These pop two values and push 1.0 (true) or 0.0 (false). Test with `3 < 5` → 1.0 (true).
hints: `LessThan`: pop b, pop a, push if a < b else 0.

steps.title: Function Call Support
steps.description: Add `Call(usize)` and `Return` opcodes. Implement a call stack (`Vec<usize>` for return addresses). Create a simple function that adds two numbers. Call it and print the result.
hints: `Call(addr)`: push current ip+1 onto call stack, set ip to addr.
Functions need local variable frames (add `call_stack: Vec<usize>`).

verification.failureMessage: Call a function that adds 3+4 and print 7.

steps.title: VM with Memory
steps.description: Add memory operations: `Load(usize)` (load from memory address), `Store(usize)` (store to memory address). Implement a `memory: Vec<f64>` array. Store and retrieve values.
hints: `memory: Vec<f64>` can be a fixed-size array.

verification.failureMessage: Store 42 at address 0, load it back, and print.

steps.title: Full VM with Program
steps.description: Write a more complex program: compute factorial(5) recursively using the VM. Print the result (120). Show the bytecode and the execution.
hints: Factorial: if n <= 1 return 1, else return n * factorial(n-1).
Use Call/Return for recursion, comparisons for the base case.
This demonstrates your VM is Turing-complete!

verification.failureMessage: Write a factorial program, run it, and print 120.
